This website will walk you through the tutorials for the *Introduction to R* course of Ecole Polytechnique's Master program.

You are all fluent users of large language models, and an LLM will write R code faster than any of us. So this class is not about teaching you to type code from memory. It has three objectives:

1.  **Read, run and modify** R code rather than write it from scratch.
2.  **Debug** code, and in particular diagnose the errors that do not announce themselves, including in code produced by an LLM.
3.  **Organise a project** so that someone else can reproduce your results from your folder alone.

The statistics and the econometrics you already know. What we add here is the craft.

> **Practical information**
>
> **TA**: [Mateo Moglia](https://mateomoglia.github.io)
>
> **Schedule**: 2 sessions of 4 hours. Check Moodle before class in case of any change in classroom.
>
> **Required software**: R and its IDE, RStudio (all free). You may download it [here](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/). Create a free account to use [Overleaf](https://www.overleaf.com). Bring your own laptop or use the lab's computer. The data used in the tutorials are on Moodle.
>
> **Rules**: Send me an email if you miss the class. You are grown-up adults, I trust you to follow the class thoroughly. Do not hesitate to work in small groups.
>
> **Data**: Data are [here](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1mNXjRVWK4-5ZcgrYdNgevgxV25byMHPL?usp=sharing)
>
> **Evaluation**: No exam. At the end of session 2, send me a zipped project folder. It must contain your code, your data and your outputs, and it must run from a clean R session on a machine that is not yours. That is the whole test, and it is graded pass or fail.

::: {.callout-important}
## The one rule of this class

Code that runs is not code that is correct. A loud failure throws an error and costs you five minutes. A silent failure returns a number that is wrong and costs you a chapter. Everything we do here is aimed at the second kind.
:::

::: {.callout-caution collapse="true"}

## Class outline

**Session 1**

-   Part 0: First hand on R
    -   Discover R and its IDE, RStudio
    -   Project organisation, reading error messages, working with an LLM
    -   `tidyverse` environment and packages
-   Part 1: Open data
    -   Open, clean and merge data
    -   Checking a merge before you trust it
-   Part 2: Descriptive statistics
    -   Compute descriptive statistics
    -   Export them in `.tex`
    -   Linear regression

**Session 2**

-   Part 3: Data visualization
    -   Scatter plots
    -   Bar charts
    -   Density and box plots
-   Part 5: Debugging clinic
    -   Find the four mistakes in a script written by an LLM

**Bonus, if time allows or on your own**

-   Part 4: Spatial data manipulation
    -   Shapefiles
    -   Compute distances
    -   Maps

During sessions, I will walk you through all materials covered here. Exercises are marked in green and you are required to perform them. Every exercise has a solution you can unfold, but unfold it after you have tried, not before. Copying a solution you have not attempted is exactly the habit this class exists to break.

## About this site and my inspirations

I created this site for teaching purposes. It is of course perfectible and any constructive comment is more than welcome ([write me an email!](mailto:mateo.moglia@gmail.com)). I took inspiration from these sources:

-   The great [Florian Oswald](https://floswald.github.io) teaching material at Sciences Po. Do not hesitate to check his teaching material (in English)

-   The [tutorials](https://mtes-mct.github.io/parcours-r/) of the French Ministry of Ecology (in French)

-   The infamous online book [Econometrics with R](https://www.econometrics-with-r.org) (in English)
